chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub ibn Fays, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, that Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:

"There is no harm if the young boy calls the adhan before he reaches puberty, and there is no harm if the muezzin calls the adhan while he is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub), but he does not call the iqamah until he performs the ritual bath (ghusl)."

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And if a need arises for the muezzin that requires speech other than the adhan, he should speak it, but it is not permissible for him to speak during the iqamah when he has the choice.

key_terms.الْاخْتِيَارِ: choice / when one has the option
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: in a state of major ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Can the muezzin call the adhan while in a state of major ritual impurity (junub)?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia juristic distinction between the adhan and iqamah, where the adhan is considered a public proclamation less sensitive to minor interruptions or impurity, whereas the iqamah requires greater solemnity and ritual purity. It specifically notes that while a *junub* (one in major impurity) may call the adhan, he must perform *ghusl* before calling the iqamah, and that brief speech is permissible during the adhan but invalidates the iqamah if done voluntarily. This reflects the broader Shia principle that the adhan serves as a call to prayer for the community, while the iqamah marks the immediate commencement of the prayer itself, demanding higher ritual integrity.
